- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per positive sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply 1–2% downward correction for days 25–30 if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., negative → positive → negative), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true reversal.
